<!-- pr-reviewer: fabf04253f899055a13ac1258dbe579ac86a48f0 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The fix is sound. The file has three small gaps in its life cycle.

**What looks good**
- The cause is plausible. The pipe write end is inherited by a process that outlives cargo (the sccache server), and no watchdog runs during the reader join. A file has no end-of-file wait.
- The JSON is read only after `watchdog::wait` returns, so the read never races cargo. `exec.rs:277` uses the JSON only when `code == 0`. A stalled or failed build (code -1 or not 0) never uses a partial record.
- The watchdog still covers the whole build. It counts the size of the open handle (`probe`) as output, as it counted pipe bytes before.
- The name is unique for each step: process id plus an atomic counter (`direct.rs:213-217`).
- A cargo failure keeps its diagnostic: the exit code, and stderr in the step log.
- The code uses only `std::fs` and `std::process`. No `cfg` arm is added.
- The decision file is complete. It says that the cause is probable, not confirmed, and it names the dropped options. The body has `Process change: yes`, and `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is untouched by the PR. The commit subject is a conventional one.

**Results (locally, merged with origin/main 4e7929dfe; the trial merge was clean)**
- `cargo test -j 6 -p xtask --bin xtask` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`): 330 passed, 0 failed. This includes `watchdog_tests::a_recording_build_ends_when_cargo_exits_not_when_its_descendants_do`.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- After the run, no `xtask-cargo-json-*` or `xtask-watchdog-orphan-*` entry was left in the temporary directory (Windows 11).
- `xtask/tests/catalog.rs`: not run (it builds camcraft-cli and times out). Linux and macOS: not run here.
- Runner: not used. The PR touches `xtask/`, which the workflow refuses.
- Heavy lanes: not run. Main's rule for the heavy lanes (#3556) asks for none at review, and xtask reaches none.

**Requested before merge**

Class: the lifecycle of the JSON file is not owned by one thing. Three cases show it. One rule closes the class: create the file with `create_new(true)`, hold it in a guard whose `Drop` removes it on every exit, and treat any I/O failure of the file as "nothing recorded". Then put the file where an abnormal exit is also covered, for example beside the step log (`log_dir`, a name that already is unique for each step and run) instead of a shared temporary directory.

1. `xtask/src/direct.rs:191-197`. The file is leaked on a path that returns early. `out.try_clone().map_err(fail)?` (line 194) and the spawn error (line 195-197 path) are fine, but the clone failure returns before the removal at line 202. A hard kill of xtask (Ctrl-C on Windows, SIGKILL) also leaves the file, and nothing sweeps it. A Drop guard covers the first case. The log directory covers the second.
2. `xtask/src/direct.rs:191`. `File::create` in the shared temporary directory follows a symlink at a predictable name (`<pid>-<n>`). On a shared Linux host, another user can point it at a file of the gate user. Use `OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true)`. `create_new` refuses an existing name or a symlink.
3. `xtask/src/direct.rs:191-192, 200, 204`. A create or read error of this file now ends the step with `Err`, and `exec.rs:274` aborts the gate or the lane with `?`. The recording is optional: `exec.rs:283` already has the path "no test executable recorded; its steps start cargo". Before the PR, no file error was possible. Return the exit code with an empty or `None` JSON and a note, not an `Err`. A failed build then still reports its own result.
4. Test. The new test pins the bounded end. It does not pin the removal. Add one assertion: after `direct::cargo` returns, no file `xtask-cargo-json-<pid>-*` (or the file beside the log) remains. Do it for the green case and for a stalled case (a short `limit`, helper mode `silent`). On Windows a descendant that holds the file must not make the assertion flaky: the run here showed the name gone at once.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The test bound (30 s against a 120 s descendant, a 60 s limit) is wide enough. A slow start of the helper will not flake it. If the kill by pid fails, the descendant ends by itself after 120 s.
- The reported wedge is not reproduced, so the cause stays probable. The PR body says to reopen #3675 if it returns. That is the right handling.
- `xtask-watchdog-orphan-<pid>` is removed with `let _`. If the kill is late on Windows, the directory can stay. This is only a note.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: ed4612b520d79e19cc2aec7d8d0f7d285664f16a -->
Delta re-review of the review at fabf04253. Head: ed4612b52.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Each finding of the old review is closed by the one rule, and a test pins each one.

## The four findings against the rule

1. The file leaked on an early return and on a hard kill. Closed. `direct::JsonFile` has a `Drop` that removes the file (`xtask/src/direct.rs`). The guard exists from the `create_new` call to the return of `cargo`, so green, red, failed-start and early-return exits all remove the file. The file is now `<step log>.json` in the run's own log directory (`direct::json_path`). A hard kill of xtask can still leave it, but only in that run's directory and not in a shared one. This is accepted. Pinned by `a_recording_build_ends_when_cargo_exits_not_when_its_descendants_do` (green build, with a descendant that still holds the file) and `the_json_file_is_removed_after_a_failed_build_and_a_failed_start` (red build, and a cargo that cannot start).
2. `File::create` followed a link at a predictable name. Closed. `JsonFile::create` uses `OpenOptions::create_new(true)`. An entry at the name is an error, and the guard does not exist then, so the entry is not written and not removed. Pinned by `an_entry_at_the_json_name_is_not_followed`. Note: the test plants a regular file, not a link. `create_new` refuses a link by the same rule, so this is enough.
3. An I/O error aborted the gate. Closed. A create, clone or read error gives `Some(Err(why))`. The build then runs with its stdout dropped. `exec.rs` prints "no test executable of <crate> recorded (<why>); its steps start cargo". Pinned by `an_io_error_of_the_json_file_records_nothing_and_the_build_still_runs`.
4. No test pinned the removal. Closed by the three tests above, each of which asserts `!path.exists()` after the call.

## What looks good
- The decision record `docs/decisions/3675-prebuild-json-file.md` states the rule and the dropped options.
- The change is small and in one place (`direct::cargo`, plus a two-line call site in `exec.rs`). No `unwrap` or `expect` in the new non-test code.
- Process: the body has `Process change: yes`, a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #3675`. The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `build.rs`, any `Cargo.toml` or `.github/`.

## Results, merged with current origin/main (trial merge, locally; it merged without conflict)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -j 6 -p xtask --bin xtask` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6) | 333 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `xtask/tests/catalog.rs` | not run (as ordered) |

Heavy lanes: not run. The change is xtask only, and the maintainer ordered no heavy lanes for this re-review.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
- The cold sccache server path was not run end to end (the author says so in the body). The cause is the probable one, not a confirmed one. If the wedge comes back, #3675 reopens.
- The PR is a draft. Under the rule of #3728, the author's push after a finding does not need a draft round trip. The merging session flags it ready.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
